item.text:
**Source map — IMP-001, CONEVAL Comunicado No. 10, "Evaluación de Procesos del Programa Sembrando Vida" (20-Sep-2022), units 1–6**

Document identity & role
- Comunicado No. 10, dated 20-Sep-2022, México City. Issuing body: Consejo Nacional de Evaluación de la Política de Desarrollo Social (CONEVAL), Dirección de Información y Comunicación Social. Role: press release announcing publication of the process evaluation. (p1)
- Underlying product is a process (not impact) evaluation of Programa Sembrando Vida (PSV); CONEVAL states it has technical and management autonomy and norm/coordinates evaluation of national social-development policy. (p1, p5 "SOBRE EL CONEVAL")
- CONEVAL's stated purpose: "fortalecimiento de la política nacional de desarrollo social mediante la generación de información útil para la toma de decisiones." (p1)

Evaluation design & methods
- Type: qualitative process evaluation combining gabinete analysis and fieldwork; analytical sample selected on qualitative criteria (operational progress, operating context, component interaction, beneficiary concentration). (p2 "Metodología")
- Period framing: "a tres años de su implementación" and built on a 2019 Diseño con Trabajo de Campo evaluation. (p1)
- Scope extends to (a) COVID-era operational changes, (b) operational articulation with Producción para el Bienestar (PPB) and Precios de Garantía (PPG). (p1, p4–5)
- Limitations disclosed by the release: analytical-not-statistical sample; no impact attribution offered; findings restricted to "procesos" (operations). (p2)

Program design & scale (as described in the release)
- Objective: subjects of right (SD) in municipalities with Rezago Social to have 2.5 ha under Sistemas Agroforestales (SAF) / Milpa Intercalada entre Árboles Frutales (MIAF) and basic food needs covered. (p2)
- Benefits: MXN 5,000/month cash, in-kind supports, social/technical accompaniment; organized in Comunidades de Aprendizaje Campesino (CAC) of 25 SDs operating Viveros Comunitarios and Biofábricas. (p2)
- Implementing agency: Secretaría de Bienestar; PPB and PPG implemented by Sader; PSV, PPB, PPG designated Programas Prioritarios para el Bienestar since 2019. (p2)
- 2021 coverage cited: 450,099 persons in 21 entidades federativas; 743+ million trees planted (62% of 1,188 million programmed); 1,089,210 ha reforested; 18,108 CAC; 14,621 Viveros Comunitarios and equal number of Biofábricas. (p2)

Implementation findings
- Strengths: clear norms for beneficiary selection and monthly padrón updates; integration of CACs into "Distrito CAC" cells; technical accompaniment flagged by SDs as fundamental. (p2, p3–4)
- Weaknesses in planeación: limited field-staff input on productive goals, MIAF/SAF and plant counts, generating work-plan adjustments, beneficiary concern over plantation upkeep, and potential water-demand pressures. (p3)
- Weaknesses in producción/distribución/entrega: observed local supply shortfalls for vivero/biofábrica inputs (e.g., plastic bags); some plants supplied by Secretaría de la Defensa Nacional lacked technical characteristics for plot transfer (climate-fit, timing); missing concentration/distribution infrastructure raising costs for técnicos/beneficiaries; banking bottlenecks at Banco del Bienestar (few/unserviceable ATMs, teller saturation) for the MXN 5,000 payment. (p3–4)
- Weaknesses in CAC implementation: most CACs formed after 2019 lack the three Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro becarios stipulated in norms; técnicos report S-Núcleo reporting as workload overload. (p4)
- Monitoring/evaluation weakness: PSV's Matriz de Indicadores para Resultados (MIR) lacks indicators tied to social aspects and to "suficiencia alimentaria." (p4–5)

COVID-19 adjustments observed
- Affected production, distribution/delivery, and monitoring; suspended CAC meetings/training; rescheduled activities to avoid same-day co-location; caused temporary slowdown. (p5)

Articulation with PPB/PPG
- Possible overlap in target population identified; recommended joint technical assistance via biofertilizers/agroecological systems; maize from MIAF plots, after family consumption, could be channeled through Precios de Garantía. (p5)
- Footnote 1 notes Programa S292 Fertilizantes (Sader, 2022: Chiapas, Guerrero, Morelos, Puebla, Tlaxcala) targets similar populations but was excluded from the articulation analysis. (p2)

Distributional & inclusion observations
- CACs integrate women under a gender-equity and rotation scheme (cited as strength). (p4)
- Banking bottlenecks and infrastructure gaps create de facto exclusion costs for beneficiaries. (p3–4)

Corrections / recommendations (release-level)
- Strengthen MIAF/SAF planning with field staff and define min/max planting ranges; build regional supplier portfolios and timing plans; review Defensa Nacional plant quality/timing; explore local-convention logistics spaces; improve Banco del Bienestar linkages and card use; promote Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro participation; reduce S-Núcleo burden on técnicos; build MIR indicators for social and food-sufficiency dimensions. (p3–5)

Qualifications carried in the text
- Descriptive and procedural findings only; no causal or impact claims made by CONEVAL in this release. (p1–5)
- "Fortalezas" and "áreas de oportunidad" are evaluator assertions grounded in qualitative fieldwork and gabinete review. (p1–4)
- Coverage/beneficiary/tree figures are program administrative outputs reported in the release, not independently audited here. (p2)
- COVID adjustments described as temporary process changes, not outcome changes. (p5)

Limitations flagged for downstream use
- Process evaluation; cannot establish impact, durability, or attribution to macro outcomes. (p1–2)
- No comparator group or counterfactual analysis offered in the release. (p2)
- FINDER-level data on income, migration, or productivity absent; food-sufficiency outcome left unmeasured per CONEVAL's own MIR critique. (p4–5)
- Independence: CONEVAL's technical/management autonomy is self-declared in the boilerplate; autonomy does not by itself establish neutrality. (p5)

Likely opposing material (not present in extract; for later chapters)
- No counter-evidence on leakage, clientelism, deforestation risk, or post-subsidy sustainability is presented in the release itself. (p1–6)
- Sections a stronger model should reopen: independent verification of the 2021 coverage/tree figures; mortality of Defensa Nacional-sourced plants; distributional incidence across estados; effectiveness of Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro integration; reliability of S-Núcleo data given reported overload. (p2–4)

Source role (recap)
- Autonomous_evaluator release from CONEVAL; treat as official evaluator description of program operations, not as outcome or impact evidence. (p1–5)
